scenes.narration: R I P is the oldest routing protocol still on the exam. It counts steps and nothing else. It's simple, slow, and still tested.

scenes.heading: The town crier
scenes.narration: In a quiet village, every resident knows only their neighbours. Every thirty seconds, the town crier walks round shouting every house they know and how many steps away it is. You write it down and add one step. That count is the hop count. Fifteen steps is the limit, and sixteen means unreachable. It's simple, but a long road takes forever to hear about.

scenes.heading: Setting up RIPv2
scenes.narration: To set it up, use version two. Turn off auto summary. Advertise your networks. And check with show I P protocols.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. R I P version two uses multicast, not broadcast. You can turn off auto summary with one command. And R I P uses U D P port five twenty, not T C P.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. R I P counts hops, and sixteen means unreachable. Use version two, and turn off auto summary. It updates every thirty seconds over U D P. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva RIP lab.
